audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagreed with its own whys on six of seven rows: it gave Gragas levels 2 and 3 while whys[1] and whys[2] call both a skill trade, gave Skill at 4-5 and 6 while whys[3] says 'Gragas takes over at 4-5' and whys[4] calls 6 his swing, and gave him 2+ items while whys[6] says late 'flattens back to even'.
audit.why: The content prose was already correct and matches the packet chart; only the tokens were stale. The mirror audit flipped its side onto the same chart with ratings 3-5-5-7-7-7-5.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Maokai / Skill / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Skill as one atomic group of matched full+content pairs, with ratings 7/5/5/3/3/3/5 — the inverse of the mirror's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every phase why in the full layer was untouched boilerplate with no spike named and no number in it.
audit.why: The real spike structure is legible from the kit: Maokai owns level 1 because Barrel Roll costs 80 mana and only sustains, Gragas takes over at 4-5 on Body Slam plus Happy Hour, level 6 is Explosive Cask on 100s, and first item is his AP brawl window.
audit.corrected: All seven phase whys rewritten with the real ability names, costs and cooldowns, each matching its new stage owner.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects is right: the full layer never names a single Gragas ability except Body Slam, and nothing anywhere mentions that Drunken Rage is a one-second channel he must stand still for, on a 5-second cooldown.
audit.why: That channel is the cleanest engage cue in the lane — a Maokai watching for it gets a free Twisted Advance at 525 into a rooted target, which is worth far more than 'track Body Slam'. Happy Hour also heals him on every skill cast, which is why anti-heal is core here rather than optional.
audit.corrected: Drunken Rage's channel and 5s cooldown written into phases[2].why, breakdown.cooldowns and tradeGood; Happy Hour and the Grievous Wounds timing written into phases[3].why; Barrel Roll's 80 mana cost into phases[0].why and whys[0].

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Gragas contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours: Barrel Roll costs 80 mana and only sustains him. Walk up on his empty bar and take free auto trades.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Gragas's Body Slam is down.
edits.after: Skill window: Body Slam is 14s and 600 range against your 525 W. Whoever lands their engage first owns the trade.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gragas must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Drunken Rage is a 1-second stand-still channel on 5s — that pause is your cue to W in, root, and Q him off the wave.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Body Slam's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: He takes 4-5: Body Slam picks the trade and Happy Hour heals him every cast. Buy Grievous Wounds early or the grind stalls.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gragas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Explosive Cask lands from 1000 range on 100s and knocks you back off him. Do not commit while it is up; it undoes the whole engage.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Body Slam's cooldown.
edits.after: His item, not yours — Drunken Rage cuts damage and his AP brawl beats your first tank piece.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Gragas carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on it flattens: he edges the 1v1, you own the 5v5 with Nature's Grasp and a root chain his kit cannot answer.

edits.before: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — His engage. W-peel after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — 14s, 600 range, stuns. Step up only after he spends it. - Drunken Rage is a 1-second channel on 5s: that stand-still is your engage cue. - Explosive Cask: 100s knockback.

edits.before: W-root Gragas the moment his answer is down, Q-knockback the follow-up, and let brush saplings tax his every path.
edits.after: W-root him during the Drunken Rage channel, Q-knockback him out of his own barrel, and sapling the brush he wants to pool in.

edits.before: At Level 1 you both have one ability, but his Q pool only sustains — you have no combo to fear yet, so deny his last-hits and set up your level 2 spike.
edits.after: Level 1 is mine: Barrel Roll costs 80 mana and only sustains, so I can walk up and auto-trade with Sap Magic while he pays for every cast.

notes: The content layer already named every Gragas ability correctly, so packet.defects ('never names any of Gragas's abilities') is really a full-layer defect — that is where the names were missing, and that is where I put them. One claim already on the page I could not verify and deliberately left standing rather than strengthen: that Explosive Cask can knock Maokai out of the Twisted Advance dash. Riot's W text says he is untargetable while dashing, which covers damage but says nothing about displacement, and displacement-during-untargetable-dash is exactly the class of thing the kit files do not carry. I wrote the cask knockback as 'knocks you back off him' after arrival, which is true either way.
